target_customer: Law firms, in-house compliance teams, government vendors, and regulatory affairs teams
problem: Tracking new and proposed laws across countries, obscure local sites and languages is manual and takes around 100 hours per project, per the company.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for regulatory research and alerts (pricing not found)

founders.name: Natalie Aresta-Katz
founders.background_notes: Got the idea at Paul, Weiss, per the YC page.

founders.name: Ethan Shea
founders.background_notes: Built the observability backend and first Vercel Agent per the YC page.

competitors.name: Regology
competitors.what: AI regulatory intelligence and change tracking across jurisdictions
competitors.traction_then: Now marketed as Regology by Bloomberg

competitors.name: Ascent RegTech (AscentAI)
competitors.what: Regulatory change management focused on financial services

competitors.name: Compliance.ai
competitors.what: Regulatory change monitoring mapped to internal controls

technical_complexity.rationale: Crawling obscure government sources in many languages and producing cited analysis is standard AI engineering with hard data coverage work.

defensibility.rationale: Coverage of hard to find sources could accumulate into a data advantage, but incumbents and law publishers can replicate coverage.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent tools were adding AI by 2026; no action against Regbase found.

market_need_then: Rising volume of AI, privacy and data center laws across US states and countries increased tracking work; lawyers bill many hours on manual research.

branding.domain_note: Uses regbase.com; X handle is theregbase.

identity.visual_style: Product site with an interactive data center regulation map
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and direct, stressing speed, reliability and catching what others miss

branding.brand_signature: Headline claim of turning 100 hour projects into 1 hour tasks, and the data center regulation map
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by runtimewire and Poets and Quants in 2026; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is descriptive and memorable enough, and the founder story got press, but the brand has little recognition so far.

outcome_analysis: Regbase is a Spring 2026 company with no exit. It reports Fortune 500 and law firm customers on its site, announced an undisclosed seed backed by Long Journey and Y Combinator, and has a founder with direct regulatory research experience. Competitors already sell regulatory change tracking, so differentiation rests on source coverage.
notes: Company site confirms Long Journey and YC backing; the round stage is not stated in sources, so stage is other and amount null. FundedIQ lists 500k USD pre-seed June 2026, an aggregator only, so unverified. Founded year not found. Customer claims are the company's own.
